meta.instrument: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 - as amended up to July 14, 2026
meta.authored: Read from the held text, provision by provision. NOT generated from 'LODR Compliance Calendar and Material Events.xlsx'. Hand-authored against reference/ and every rule carries the words it came from in `quote`.
meta.scope: LODR Chapters V, V-A, VI and VI-A - the obligations of an entity that has listed NON-CONVERTIBLE securities. Excluded: Reg 49 and Reg 62B, which are applicability and definitions and create no duty; and Reg 64I, which binds the RECOGNISED STOCK EXCHANGES to monitor compliance, not the listed entity.
meta.why: Chapter V had 19 uncited provisions and Chapter VI 11. But the blocker was never the corpus - see `blocker` below.
meta.blocker: Before db/026, `ncsListed` and `hvdle` were read by lodrListingTypes and set NOWHERE: no column on companies, no field on the entity form, no importer header. They were always undefined, so every LODR rule scoped listingType ['ncs'] or ['hvdle'] was unreachable. Measured against the shipped corpus that was 20 rules that could never apply to any entity - Reg 52 (financial results for debt), Reg 53, Reg 54 (asset cover), Reg 61A, Reg 62A among them. Authoring this corpus without db/026 would have added 27 more of the same. A rule that never applies looks exactly like a rule that correctly does not apply, which is why nothing had ever reported it.
readingNotes: Reg 62C was amended in 2025 and now reads: a high value debt listed entity is one 'which only has non-convertible debt securities listed, with an outstanding value of Rupees Five Thousand Crore and above AND DOES NOT HAVE ANY LISTED SPECIFIED SECURITIES'. So an entity cannot be both equity-listed and HVDLE. Chapter V-A is the corporate governance regime for debt-only issuers that Chapter IV would otherwise never reach.

Chapter VI (Reg 63, 64) binds an entity that has listed specified securities AND non-convertible securities. That is an AND, not an OR, and it is expressed here with `listingTypeAll` - scoping it to 'ncs' alone would put it on a debt-only issuer, which does not owe it.

Working-day periods are stated and NOT computed. There is no exchange holiday calendar here, and Reg 50 and Reg 60 run BACKWARD from the meeting and the record date, so a calendar-day approximation would fall later than the regulation allows.

rules.title: Give the stock exchange at least two working days prior intimation of a board meeting on non-convertible securities
rules.detail: Give prior intimation of at least two working days, excluding the date of the intimation and the date of the meeting, of a board meeting at which any of these is to be considered: an alteration in the form or nature of the non-convertible securities or in the rights or privileges of their holders; an alteration in the date on which interest or the redemption amount is payable; fund raising by issue of non-convertible securities; and the financial results.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall give prior intimation to the stock exchange of at least two working days in advance, excluding the date of the intimation and the date of the meeting of the board of directors, about the Board meeting in which any of the following proposals is to be considered
rules.timelineText: At least two working days in advance, excluding the date of the intimation and the date of the meeting

due.when: Before a board meeting on a listed proposal

rules.evidence: Intimation to each exchange with its filing timestamp; notice of the board meeting
rules.notes: The debt counterpart of Reg 29, and the period is the same two working days. Not computed: both ends are excluded, the count is in working days with no exchange holiday calendar here, and it runs BACKWARD from the meeting - so treating working days as calendar days would place the deadline later than the regulation allows.

rules.title: Certify the status of interest, dividend, redemption or principal payment within one working day of it becoming due
rules.detail: Submit a certificate to the stock exchange on the status of payment of interest or dividend, or repayment or redemption of principal, of non-convertible securities, within one working day of it becoming due, in the manner and format specified by the Board.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall submit a certificate to the stock exchange regarding status of payment of interest or dividend or repayment or redemption of principal of non-convertible securities, within one working day of it becoming due, in the manner and format as specified by the Board from time to time
rules.frequency: On every interest, dividend or redemption due date
rules.timelineText: Within one working day of it becoming due

due.when: The interest, dividend or redemption falls due

rules.evidence: The certificate as filed with each exchange, with its date; the payment instruction and bank confirmation
rules.notes: ONE working day, and the trigger is the due date itself - not the payment. The certificate is owed whether or not the money went out, which is the point of it: a default is reported by the same certificate that reports a payment. This app holds no register of interest or redemption due dates, so the date cannot be computed from anything here.

rules.title: Obtain prior approval of the stock exchange before any material modification to the terms of the securities
rules.detail: Do not make a material modification to the structure of the non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares - in terms of coupon, conversion, redemption or otherwise - without the prior approval of the stock exchanges on which they are listed.
rules.quote: shall not make material modification without prior approval of the stock exchange(s) where the non convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares, as applicable, are listed
rules.timelineText: Prior to the modification

due.when: Before a material modification to the terms

rules.evidence: Application to each exchange; the approval received; debenture holder consent where required
rules.notes: An ORDER, not a period: the approval must precede the modification. Reg 59 is disapplied for a voluntary delisting of non-convertible securities by Reg 64A(3), which is its own chapter.

rules.title: File the draft scheme of arrangement with the stock exchanges before approaching the Tribunal
rules.detail: An entity with listed non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares that proposes a scheme of arrangement, or is involved in one, must file the draft scheme with the stock exchanges for a No-objection letter before filing it with any Court or Tribunal.
rules.quote: the listed entity that has listed non - convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares, intends to undertake a scheme of arrangement or is involved in a scheme of arrangement under sections 230 -234 and section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013, shall file the draft scheme of arrangement with the stock exchange(s), along with a non -refundable fee as specified in Schedule XI, for obtaining the No -objection letter, before filing of such scheme with the National Company Law Tribunal
rules.timelineText: Before filing the scheme with any Court or Tribunal

due.when: Before filing a scheme of arrangement with a Court or Tribunal

rules.appliesToText: Entity with listed non-convertible securities undertaking a scheme of arrangement
rules.evidence: Draft scheme as filed with each exchange; No-objection letter; record of it being placed before the Tribunal
rules.notes: The debt counterpart of Reg 37. Where the scheme is a resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code, the details are disclosed to the exchanges within one day of approval.

rules.title: Give the stock exchange at least three working days notice of a record date
rules.detail: Fix the record date as required by Reg 23(7) of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations 2021, and give the recognised stock exchanges notice in advance of at least three working days, excluding the date of intimation and the record date, or as many days as the exchanges require, specifying the purpose of the record date.
rules.quote: shall give notice in advance of at least three working days (excluding the date of intimation and the record date) to the recognised stock exchange (s) of the record date or of as many days as the stock exchange(s) may agree to or require specifying the purpose of the record date
rules.timelineText: At least three working days in advance, excluding the date of intimation and the record date

due.when: Before every record date for non-convertible securities

rules.appliesToText: Entity with listed non-convertible securities fixing a record date
rules.evidence: Intimation to each exchange with its filing timestamp; board or committee resolution fixing the record date
rules.notes: Three working days, the same figure Reg 42 now carries for equity - but note Reg 60 adds 'or as many days as the stock exchange(s) may agree to or require', so an exchange can demand more and the regulation's three days is a floor, not the answer. Not computed: working days, both ends excluded, counted backward from the record date.

rules.title: Pay interest, dividend and redemption on time, and declare no dividend while in default
rules.detail: Ensure timely payment of interest or dividend on non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares, and of redemption amounts. The entity may not declare or distribute any dividend where it has defaulted in payment of interest on debt securities or in redemption, or in creating the security as per the terms of issue, for so long as the default continues.
rules.quote: shall ensure timely payment of i nterest or dividend of non- convertible debt securities and/or non-convertible redeemable preference shares or redemption payment
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Payment records against the terms of issue; board record of any dividend declared and the default position at that date
rules.notes: The proviso is the limb a Company Secretary has to catch: an entity in default on debt interest, redemption or security creation MAY NOT declare or distribute a dividend while that default subsists. It is a bar on the equity dividend arising from the debt, and it is easy to miss because it sits in the debt chapter.

rules.title: Comply with the Chapter V-A governance regime within six months of crossing the high value debt threshold
rules.detail: Chapter V-A applies to a listed entity which only has non-convertible debt securities listed, with an outstanding value of Rs 5,000 crore and above, and which does not have any listed specified securities. Where the outstanding value crosses that threshold during the financial year, comply with the chapter within six months of the trigger.
rules.quote: The provisions of this chapter shall apply to a listed entity which only has non-convertible debt securities listed, with an outstanding value of Rupees Five Thousand Crore and above and does not have any listed specified securities. it shall ensure compliance with these provisions within six months from the date of such trigger and the disclosures of such compliance may be made in the Corporate Governance Compliance Report on and from the third quarter, following the date of the trigger
rules.timelineText: Within six months from the date of the trigger

due.when: Outstanding listed non-convertible debt securities reach Rs 5,000 crore

rules.appliesToText: High value debt listed entity - debt-only issuer with Rs 5,000 crore or more of listed non-convertible debt securities
rules.evidence: Computation of outstanding listed NCD value; board note adopting the Chapter V-A governance requirements
rules.notes: The 2025 amendment narrowed this and the narrowing matters: a HVDLE is a debt-only issuer that DOES NOT have listed specified securities. An equity-listed entity with large listed debt is governed by Chapter IV instead, not by both. Chapter V-A exists to reach the governance of issuers Chapter IV never touches.

rules.title: Observe the cap on the number of directorships held by a director
rules.detail: The directors of a high value debt listed entity must comply with the conditions on the maximum number of directorships, including alternate directorships, held by them across companies.
rules.quote: The provisions of this regulation shall be complied with within six months from the date of the publication of Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Listing Obligations and Disclosure Req uirements ) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 in the Official Gazette or the date of Annual General Meeting, whichever is later
rules.timelineText: Within six months from the publication of the 2025 Amendment Regulations, or the date of the Annual General Meeting, whichever is later

due.when: Six months from publication of the 2025 Amendment, or the AGM, whichever is later

rules.evidence: Directorship declarations from each director; the board's record of the count across companies
rules.notes: The transition date is WHICHEVER IS LATER of two events, one of which is the entity's own AGM - so it differs per entity and cannot be a single date in this register. The Official Gazette publication date of the 2025 Amendment is not stated in the held compilation, so even the first limb cannot be computed here.

rules.title: Constitute an audit committee of at least three directors, two-thirds independent
rules.detail: Constitute an audit committee with a minimum of three directors as members, at least two-thirds of whom are independent directors, all financially literate and at least one having accounting or related financial management expertise, with the terms of reference the regulation sets.
rules.quote: Every HVDLE shall constitute an audit committee subject to the following terms of reference: (a) The audit committee shall have minimum three directors as members. (b) At least two -thirds of the members of audit committee shall be independent directors.
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Board resolution constituting the committee; composition against the two-thirds test; financial literacy record
rules.notes: Two-thirds independent, which is a higher bar than the Companies Act s.177 majority. The composition has to be re-tested on every change to the board, not only when the committee is formed.

rules.title: Discharge the nomination and remuneration committee functions
rules.detail: The board of directors must ensure that the functions of the nomination and remuneration committee specified in Part D of Schedule II are discharged, either by a constituted committee or by the board itself as the regulation permits.
rules.quote: The board of directors shall ensure that the functions of the nomination and remuneration committee as specified in Part D of the Schedule II are either discharged by
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Board resolution; committee minutes, or board minutes where the board discharges the functions itself
rules.notes: The functions are in Part D of Schedule II, which is not carried in this register. The duty is that they are DISCHARGED, which the regulation allows to happen without a separate committee.

rules.title: Discharge the stakeholders relationship committee functions
rules.detail: The board of directors must ensure that the functions of the stakeholders relationship committee specified in Part D of Schedule II are discharged.
rules.quote: The board of directors shall ensure that the functions of the stakeholders relationship committee as specified in Part D of the Schedule II are discharged by the boar
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Board resolution; record of debenture holder grievances considered and their disposal
rules.notes: For a debt-only issuer the stakeholders whose grievances this reaches are the holders of the non-convertible securities, not equity shareholders.

rules.title: Discharge the risk management committee functions
rules.detail: The board of directors must ensure that the functions of the Risk Management Committee specified in Part D of Schedule II are discharged by the audit committee, by the board, or by a committee constituted for the purpose.
rules.quote: The board of directors shall ensure that the functions of the Risk Management Committee as specified in Part D of the Schedule II are discharged by audit committee or
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Board resolution naming which body discharges the functions; minutes of the risk review
rules.notes: The regulation names three permitted routes - the audit committee, the board, or a separate committee - so the compliance question is which one, recorded, rather than whether a committee exists.

rules.title: Formulate a vigil mechanism or whistle blower policy
rules.detail: Formulate a vigil mechanism or whistle blower policy for directors and employees to report genuine concerns. It must provide adequate safeguards against victimisation of anyone who uses it, and direct access to the chairperson of the audit committee in appropriate or exceptional cases.
rules.quote: shall formulate a vigil mechanism/ whistle blower policy for directors and employees to report genuine concerns
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: The board-approved policy; evidence of the direct access route to the audit committee chairperson
rules.notes: Three separate limbs: the policy, the safeguards against victimisation, and direct access to the audit committee chairperson. A policy that omits the third does not satisfy the regulation. Distinct from the s.177(9) vigil mechanism under the Companies Act and from PIT Reg 9A(6) - an entity can owe all three.

rules.title: Comply with the related party transaction regime, except Reg 23(8) and 23(9)
rules.detail: A high value debt listed entity must comply with Reg 23 in respect of related party transactions, except Reg 23(8) and Reg 23(9).
rules.quote: HVDLE shall comply with the provisions of regulation 23 above except regulation 23(8) and regulation 23(9) in respect of related party transactions
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Related party transaction policy; audit committee approvals; the register of transactions
rules.notes: The two exclusions are the point of the rule. Reg 23(9) is the half-yearly disclosure of related party transactions to the stock exchanges, and Reg 23(8) the transitional provision - so a HVDLE applies the approval and policy machinery of Reg 23 without those two limbs. Applying Reg 23 whole would put a filing on the register that is not owed.

rules.title: Observe the obligations attaching to independent directors
rules.detail: No person may be appointed as an alternate director for an independent director. The maximum tenure of independent directors is as provided in the regulation, together with the other obligations it places on them.
rules.quote: No person shall be appointed as an alternate director for an independent director of a HVDLE
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Board resolutions on appointment; tenure record for each independent director
rules.notes: The bar on an alternate for an independent director is absolute and is the limb most often breached in practice, because appointing an alternate looks like an ordinary board act.

rules.title: Observe the cap of ten committee memberships and five chairmanships per director
rules.detail: A director must not be a member of more than ten committees, nor act as chairperson of more than five committees, across all listed entities in which they are a director. For the purpose of the limit, all public limited companies are counted as the regulation directs.
rules.quote: A director shall not be a member in more than ten committee s or act as chairperson of more than five committees across all listed entities in which he/she is a director
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.evidence: Committee membership declarations from each director, covering every company they serve
rules.notes: The count is ACROSS COMPANIES, not within this one, so it cannot be verified from this entity's own registers alone - it rests on declarations the director gives. Ten memberships and five chairmanships are separate caps and a director can breach the second while inside the first.

rules.title: Fill a vacancy in the office of CEO, MD, Whole Time Director, Manager or CFO within three months
rules.detail: Any vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager must be filled at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date of the vacancy; six months where a regulatory, government or statutory approval is needed. The same applies to the Chief Financial Officer. Where a resolution plan has been approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code, such a vacancy is filled within three months of that approval.
rules.quote: Any vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager shall be filled by the HVDLE at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date of s uch vacancy: Provided that where the HVDLE is required to obtain approval of regulatory, government or statutory authorities to fill up such vacancies, then the vacancies shall be filled up by the HVDLE at the earliest and in any case not later than six months from the date of vacancy
rules.timelineText: Not later than three months from the date of the vacancy; six months where a regulatory, government or statutory approval is required
rules.evidence: Board resolution appointing the replacement; the date the office fell vacant
rules.notes: The HVDLE counterpart of Reg 26A, with the same three and six month periods. This app holds no record of the date an office fell vacant, so the deadline is stated rather than computed.

rules.title: Comply with Chapter IV in full, and with the named Chapter V provisions in addition
rules.detail: An entity which has listed both specified securities and non-convertible securities is bound by Chapter IV of these regulations, and must additionally comply with the following provisions of Chapter V: Reg 50, Reg 51, Reg 52(3), 52(4), 52(6) and 52(7), and Regs 53 to 62.
rules.quote: shall be bound by the provisions in Chapter IV of these regulations. (2) The listed entity described in sub -regulation (1) shall additionally comply with the following regulations in Chapter V
rules.timelineText: Continuous
rules.appliesToText: Entity with both listed specified securities and listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: The compliance calendar showing both chapters applied
rules.notes: This is the mapping rule, and it is why an entity with both kinds of securities does not simply owe both chapters whole: Chapter IV applies in full, but only the NAMED provisions of Chapter V come with it. Scoping this to debt alone would put it on a debt-only issuer, which is governed by Chapter V and Chapter V-A instead.

rules.title: On a delisting of either kind of security, take up the other chapter in full
rules.detail: Where the specified securities are delisted from the stock exchange, the entity must comply with all the provisions of Chapter V. Where the non-convertible securities cease to be listed, it must comply with all the provisions of Chapter IV.
rules.quote: the listed entity shall comply with all the provisions in Chapter V of these regulations. (2) In the event that non-convertible debt securities and non -convertible redeem able preference shares' of the listed entity do not remain listed on the stock exchange, the listed entity shall comply with all the provisions in Chapter IV
rules.timelineText: On the delisting taking effect

due.when: Either class of securities ceases to be listed

rules.appliesToText: Entity with both listed specified securities and listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: The delisting order or confirmation; the revised compliance calendar
rules.notes: A delisting REMOVES the Reg 63 subset and puts the remaining chapter back in full - so the obligation set gets larger on one side at the moment it disappears on the other. A compliance calendar built for a both-listed entity is wrong from the day either class is delisted.

rules.title: Disclose a delisting under a resolution plan within one working day of the plan being approved
rules.detail: Chapter VI-A governs the voluntary delisting of listed non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares, subject to the exclusions the regulation sets out. Where the delisting is pursuant to a resolution plan under the Insolvency Code, it must be disclosed to the stock exchanges within one working day of the approval of that plan.
rules.quote: shall be disclosed to the stock exchanges where such securities or shares are listed within one working day of the approval of the resolution plan under the Insolvency Code
rules.frequency: On a delisting under a resolution plan
rules.timelineText: Within one working day of the approval of the resolution plan

due.when: Resolution plan approved under the Insolvency Code

rules.appliesToText: Entity with listed non-convertible securities delisting under a resolution plan
rules.evidence: Tribunal order approving the resolution plan; the disclosure with its filing timestamp
rules.notes: Chapter VI-A does not apply where the securities were issued by public issue, where there are more than two hundred holders excluding qualified institutional buyers, or where the delisting follows a penalty, redemption or a resolution plan. Reg 59 - prior approval for a material modification - is expressly disapplied to a voluntary delisting under this chapter.

rules.title: Apply for in-principle approval within fifteen working days of the board resolution
rules.detail: Apply to the relevant stock exchanges for in-principle approval of the proposed delisting, in the form the exchange specifies, not later than fifteen working days from the date of passing the board resolution. The exchange disposes of a complete application within fifteen working days of receiving it.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall make an application to the relevant stock exchange(s) for seeking in -principle approval for the proposed delisting of non -convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares in the form specified by such stoc k exchange, not later than fifteen working days from the date of passing of the board resolution to that effect or of receipt of any other statutory or regulatory approval, whichever is later
rules.timelineText: Not later than fifteen working days from the date of passing the board resolution, or of receipt of any other statutory or regulatory approval, whichever is later
rules.appliesToText: Entity voluntarily delisting its listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: Board resolution with its date; the application to each exchange with its date of receipt
rules.notes: Step 1 of the delisting sequence, and its clock runs from the BOARD RESOLUTION. The fifteen working days the exchange takes to dispose of the application is the exchange's period, not the entity's.

rules.title: Commence holder approval within three working days, and disclose the delisting events within two
rules.detail: Ensure the process of obtaining approval from all holders of the non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares commences within three working days of the grant of in-principle approval by the stock exchanges. Disclose the events in respect of the delisting on the website and to the stock exchanges within two working days from the date of receipt of the in-principle approval.
rules.quote: shall ensure that the process of obtaining necessary approval from all holders of non -convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares commences within three working days of the gra nt of in - principle approval by the stock exchange(s). shall be disclosed by the listed entity on its website as well as to the stock exchanges, within two working days from the date of receipt of in -principle approval from the stock exchanges for delisting of non -convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares
rules.timelineText: Commence within three working days of the in-principle approval; disclose within two working days of its receipt

due.when: In-principle approval granted by the stock exchange

rules.appliesToText: Entity voluntarily delisting its listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: In-principle approval with its date; record that the approval process commenced; the website and exchange disclosures with their dates
rules.notes: TWO periods run from the same in-principle approval and they are different lengths - two working days to disclose, three to commence the holder approval process. The disclosure is the shorter of the two, which is the opposite of the intuitive order.

rules.title: Send the notice of delisting to holders within three working days of the in-principle approval
rules.detail: Send the notice of delisting to the holders of the non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares not later than three working days from the date of receipt of the in-principle approval from the stock exchanges. A copy of the notice goes to the stock exchanges and the debenture trustee, and it must carry the name and contact details of the compliance officer.
rules.quote: shall send the notice of delisting to the holders of non -convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares , not later than three working days from the date of receipt of in -principle approval from the stock exchanges
rules.timelineText: Not later than three working days from the date of receipt of the in-principle approval

due.when: In-principle approval received from the stock exchange

rules.appliesToText: Entity voluntarily delisting its listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: The notice as despatched with its date; proof of despatch to every holder; the copy filed with the exchanges and the debenture trustee
rules.notes: This runs from RECEIPT of the in-principle approval, while Reg 64C(1)'s three days run from its GRANT. Those are not always the same day, and the notice starts the fifteen-working-day clock in Reg 64E.

rules.title: Obtain approval from all holders within fifteen working days of the notice, and a No-Objection Letter from the debenture trustee
rules.detail: Obtain approval from all the holders of the non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares within fifteen working days from the date of the notice of delisting, and obtain the No-Objection Letter from the debenture trustee in the case of a delisting of non-convertible debt securities.
rules.quote: shall obtain approval from all the holders of non -convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares within fifteen working days from the date of the notice of delisting
rules.timelineText: Within fifteen working days from the date of the notice of delisting

due.when: The notice of delisting is issued

rules.appliesToText: Entity voluntarily delisting its listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: Written approval from every holder; the debenture trustee's No-Objection Letter
rules.notes: ALL the holders, not a majority - which is why Chapter VI-A is confined to issues with two hundred holders or fewer excluding qualified institutional buyers. One holder who does not respond inside the fifteen working days fails the proposal under Reg 64F.

rules.title: Intimate a failed delisting proposal to the stock exchanges within one working day
rules.detail: A delisting proposal is deemed to have failed on non-receipt of in-principle approval, on failure to obtain the approval of all holders, or in the other circumstances the regulation names. On failure, intimate the stock exchanges within one working day from the date of the event of failure.
rules.quote: shall intimate the same to the stock exchanges within one working day from the date of event of failure as specified in sub -regulation (1)
rules.frequency: On failure of a delisting proposal
rules.timelineText: Within one working day from the date of the event of failure
rules.appliesToText: Entity voluntarily delisting its listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: Record of the failure event and its date; the intimation with its filing timestamp
rules.notes: ONE working day, and the trigger is a non-event - an approval that did not arrive. The date of failure is therefore the date a period expired rather than the date something happened, which is what makes it easy to miss.

rules.title: Make the final delisting application within five working days of obtaining holder approval
rules.detail: Within five working days from the date of obtaining the requisite approval from the holders under Reg 64E, make the final application for delisting to the stock exchange in the form it specifies. The exchange disposes of a complete application within fifteen working days of receipt.
rules.quote: Within five working days from the date of obtaining the requisite approval from the holders of non -convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares in terms of regulation 64E of these regulations, the listed entity shall make the final application for delisting to the st
rules.timelineText: Within five working days from the date of obtaining the requisite approval from the holders

due.when: Approval obtained from all holders under Reg 64E

rules.appliesToText: Entity voluntarily delisting its listed non-convertible securities
rules.evidence: The holder approvals with their dates; the final application with its date of filing
rules.notes: The last step the entity controls. The fifteen working days for disposal belongs to the stock exchange and is not a deadline on the company.

rules.title: Delisting from some exchanges while staying on one: Reg 64B to 64G do not apply, but board approval and an application do
rules.detail: Where the non-convertible debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares are listed on more than one stock exchange, the entity may choose to delist them from all exchanges except one having nationwide trading terminals. Where it does, Reg 64B to 64G do not apply; instead the entity must obtain the prior approval of its board of directors for the delisting and make an application to the stock exchange to delist.
rules.quote: Where the non -convertible debt securities or non -convertible redeemable preference shares are listed on more than one stock exchanges, the listed entity may choose to delist such sec urities or shares from all stock exchanges except one such stock exchange having nationwide trading terminals. If the listed entity proposes to delist its non -convertible debt securities or non - convertible redeemable preference shares as per sub -regulati on (1), the provisions of regulations 64B to 64G of these regulations shall not be applicable and the listed entity shall: (a) obtain the prior approval of its board of directors for such delisting; (b) make an application to the stock exchange for delisting its non -convertible de
rules.timelineText: On the delisting

due.when: Delisting from some of the stock exchanges

rules.appliesToText: Entity with listed non-convertible securities on more than one stock exchange
rules.evidence: The delisting applications and confirmations per exchange
rules.notes: This is an EXEMPTION, not a variation, and reading it as one more step in the sequence gets it backwards: keep a listing on one nationwide exchange and the whole Reg 64B to 64G machinery - in-principle approval, notice to holders, approval from ALL holders, the final application - falls away, leaving board approval and an application. Remaining listed on that one exchange also keeps the whole of Chapter V alive, so the compliance calendar does not shrink. Reg 64I, which requires the exchanges to monitor compliance with this chapter and report to the Board, binds the EXCHANGES and is not carried here.
